trust_decision.summary: LZ4DecompressorWithLength trusts the 4-byte little-endian length prefix of attacker-supplied data as the output size (allocation size, or write length into a caller buffer) with no bound against the input size, a maximum, or the destination capacity.

landing_point.why: The summary names LZ4DecompressorWithLength and a 1 GiB allocation from the length header; the allocating decompress(byte[], int) reads the header and hands it straight to the allocating fast-decompressor call.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API LZ4DecompressorWithLength.decompress(byte[]) / decompress(byte[], int) with fast decompressor (allocating)
public API LZ4DecompressorWithLength.decompress(byte[], int, int) with safe decompressor (allocating; also reached from decompress(byte[]) and decompress(byte[], int))
public API decompress(byte[], byte[]) / decompress(byte[], int, byte[], int), fast path (caller-provided dest, no capacity check)
public API decompress(byte[], int, int, byte[], int), safe path (caller-provided dest)
public API decompress(ByteBuffer, ByteBuffer) (position-moving; both paths)
public API decompress(ByteBuffer, int, ByteBuffer, int), fast path
public API decompress(ByteBuffer, int, int, ByteBuffer, int), safe path
public constructors; fix adds overloads with a configurable maxDecompressedLength (fix.diff:77-121)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published source changes are in src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4DecompressorWithLength.java (fix.diff:5-226). The allocating primitives src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4FastDecompressor.java:109-110 and src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4SafeDecompressor.java:117-118 take a caller-supplied length and were not changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: LZ4BlockInputStream is a different on-wire format (LZ4Block stream, not the 4-byte-prefixed WithLength format) and already validates its header (src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4BlockInputStream.java:260-267), so a solver can argue it is a separate, already-hardened feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The configured maximum must limit only methods that allocate their output; caller-provided-buffer methods must still decompress outputs larger than the maximum (published test configuredMaximumOnlyLimitsAllocatedOutput, fix.diff:318-330). Highly compressible legitimate data (ratio up to 255:1, fix.diff:23-24, 129-135) and zero-length outputs (fix.diff:340-344) must still decompress. A blanket 64 MiB cap on every method, or a tight ratio bound, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: declared length larger than possible for the input size (ratio > 255)
declared length above the default 64 MiB cap
declared length larger than the caller-provided byte[] dest from destOff
declared length larger than ByteBuffer dest.remaining() (position-moving overload)
declared length larger than ByteBuffer dest.capacity()-destOff (indexed overloads)

O7_producer.where: Length is parsed inline by getDecompressedLength at src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4DecompressorWithLength.java:52-54 and :73-75; no schema/serializer/cache layer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: LZ4BlockInputStream.refill() allocates compressedBuffer from the header compressedLen, which is only checked to be >= 0 (no upper bound relative to originalLen or maxCompressedLength), so a 21-byte header can request a ~2 GiB allocation before any data is read.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different stream format and class from the advisory; its header already has a validation block and originalLen is capped by 1 << compressionLevel, so it looks hardened. Strictly, it is a different allocation sink with the same property (allocation sized by an unvalidated header length), not the advisory's own sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (net.jpountz.lz4), different file and class

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a size taken from the frame descriptor or block header used for an allocation without the existing blockSize > maxBlockSize check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the frame reader already parses several size fields from the header (src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4FrameInputStream.java:221-223, 287-288), so a maintainer could plausibly drop or reorder one bound

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted companion helper (for example a stream or ByteBuffer convenience reader for the WithLength format) that calls getDecompressedLength and then the allocating LZ4FastDecompressor.decompress(src, srcOff, destLen) directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getDecompressedLength is public and static (src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4DecompressorWithLength.java:41-75), and the package docs show the read-length-then-allocate idiom (src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/package.html:45)

O9_family: CWE-789 memory allocation with excessive size value (untrusted length header); fix also adds destination-capacity checks for caller-buffer overloads

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (pom.xml), JUnit 5.9 / JUnit 4 vintage, multi-release compile; native libs can be extracted from the published 1.8.0 jar (pom.xml:10) or built with gcc (pom.xml:67-70)
O10_build.project_tests: src/test/net/jpountz/lz4/OutOfBoundsTest.java (fix adds impossibleDeclaredLength, destinationBufferLimitsDecompressedLength, configuredMaximumOnlyLimitsAllocatedOutput, configuredMaximumValidation); src/test/net/jpountz/lz4/AbstractLZ4Test.java:157-296 round-trips through LZ4DecompressorWithLength

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a single `if (destLen < 0 || destLen > LIMIT) throw` in decompress(byte[], int) and decompress(byte[], int, int), or a global cap in getDecompressedLength, leaving the caller-buffer and ByteBuffer overloads unchecked or wrongly capping them.

out_of_scope_notes: LZ4FastDecompressor/LZ4SafeDecompressor allocating overloads (src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4FastDecompressor.java:109-110, src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4SafeDecompressor.java:117-118) trust a caller-supplied length by design; not a flaw on their own.
Deprecated JNI fast decompressor writing past a caller buffer when destLen exceeds capacity is the memory-safety side of the dest checks; not pursued.
